headline: Google's Gemini App Surges Past 1 Billion Monthly Users
summary: The AI product is now the 14th Google service to reach the billion-user milestone, rivaling OpenAI's ChatGPT.
details: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announced that the Gemini app has surpassed 1 billion monthly active users, marking it as one of the company's fastest-growing products. This achievement places Gemini among Google's elite services that have reached this significant user base.

Gemini's rapid ascent mirrors that of OpenAI's ChatGPT, which also reached 1 billion monthly active users in June. Google has been actively integrating Gemini across its ecosystem, including Search, Workspace, and Android.

The AI Mode in Google Search alone boasts over 1 billion monthly active users globally. However, the 1 billion figure for Gemini specifically refers to its standalone app usage, excluding users from other integrated channels.

Google continues to enhance Gemini with new models like Gemini 3.5 Flash, optimized for coding and autonomous AI-agent tasks. User engagement data shows 63% of Gemini users interact via voice, and the platform generates over 150 million images daily.

Gemini's reach extends beyond Google's own platforms, with over 100 million active users on iOS. This milestone follows Google's Q2 2026 earnings call, where the company reported over 950 million monthly users across its services, with daily active users tripling year-over-year.
The announcement comes just before Google's upcoming Made by Google event, where further Gemini-powered features for Pixel devices are anticipated.

headline_marked: Zoom screen-sharing bug [[allows full device takeover]]
headline: Zoom screen-sharing bug allows full device takeover
summary: A critical vulnerability in Zoom's screen-sharing feature could let attackers remotely execute malicious code and take control of a user's device without any warning.
details: Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered a severe bug in Zoom's screen-sharing functionality that allows attackers to gain full control of a victim's device. This vulnerability affects Zoom Workspace apps across Windows, Mac, iOS, Android, and Linux.

The exploit requires no action from the victim and provides no visible warning. By launching the annotation tool during a screen-sharing session, attackers can remotely execute malicious code, effectively hijacking the user's machine.

Researchers used AI prompts to develop a proof-of-concept exploit in under 24 hours, highlighting how artificial intelligence can accelerate the creation of sophisticated cyberattacks. This capability, previously exclusive to nation-state actors, is now accessible to a wider range of malicious actors.

Zoom has been notified of the vulnerability and has released updates to address the issue. The company urges users to apply the latest updates to their Zoom Workspace applications to mitigate the threat. The vulnerability existed in all versions prior to these recent patches.

This incident is similar to recent security issues affecting Apple devices, which also prompted the release of macOS updates. Users are advised to ensure their systems are up-to-date to protect against such threats.
